answer: Agents could reserve scarce jobs through a commit-and-reveal auction: each vertex posts a bond before bids are opened, then reveals its bid after the deadline. A contract awards the job to the best eligible offer and slashes bonds from identities that fail to reveal or violate the rules. One person can still create many identities, but each must lock real capital, so sybil bids multiply the attacker’s cost and expose more funds to penalties. The ledge is that cheap identities alone no longer buy influence; a plume of fake accounts becomes expensive to sustain.
